analysis.title: U.S. Equities Color: Underwhelming (29 Oct 2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 closed -30bps at 7,720 with a $9bn market-on-close imbalance to buy. NDX -138bps at 29,402, R2K +75bps at 2,852, Dow -25bps at 52,342. Volume was 16.695bn shares vs a year-to-date daily average of 18.489bn.

Broader tech sold off after underwhelming overnight tech earnings. AMZN fell about 4% in the regular session and about 10% after hours on AWS growth of 39% in the quarter vs consensus above 40%. Management guided in the press release to AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028.

S&P Equal Weight and cyclical/rate-sensitive parts of the market outperformed, helped by a benign PCE print. NDX underperformed the broader market by about 2.5 points, consistent with an ongoing rotation out of tech.

Consumer caught a larger bid, partly from the rotation out of tech and partly from covering in under-owned names (NCLH, CROX, BOOT). Restaurants showed better fundamentals this week: CMG +8% today, EAT and WING the prior day, SBUX reporting after the close.

Desk activity was 5 on a 1-10 scale. Asset managers finished as slight net sellers (supply in communication services and discretionary, demand in macro). Hedge fund flows were roughly flat. Single-stock activity did not rise despite the size of the moves, and trading was top-down, with SPX volumes about 35% above the 20-day average.

Google's disappointing earnings stifled emerging optimism on the AI trade. The AI complex (GSTMTAIP) fell 1.5% and was used as a source of funds for everything else (SPXXAI +1.5%), while moderate SPX moves failed to fully capture the AI complex.

Implied volatility fell for most of the session. QQQ front-month fixed-strike vols were offered down about a vol point at the lows and SPY vols fell more than 80 bps of vol. VIX futures moved lower in nominal terms, which the desk reads as vol premium coming out of the market after several large tech prints. Skew was bid on the move lower, particularly in SPX gamma tenors.
The S&P implied move through tomorrow is 0.70%.
After-hours earnings moves: INTC -17%, PINS -16%, TWLO -15%, RBLX -10%, RDDT -5% (from -12%), SNDK unchanged, SBUX -0.7%.

Down 17% after hours. Q3 DCAI revenue grew 78% y/y, but Q4 revenue guidance of $15-16bn is well below the $17.29bn consensus. The company expects the PC slowdown to continue at least through H1 of next year.
Down 16% after hours. Q3 revenue of $1.17bn missed the $1.2bn consensus, and Q4 revenue and EBITDA guidance is below the Street.
Down 15% after hours. Q3 organic revenue grew 16% y/y, a slight slowdown from 17% last quarter. Q4 organic growth is guided to 11-12% y/y, in line with the initial Q3 organic guide.
Down 10% after hours. The company guided Q4 bookings down 10-15% y/y.
Down 5% after hours (from -12%). Q3 revenue grew 53% y/y, but US DAUs of 50.7mn fell from about 53mn last quarter. Q4 revenue guidance of $1-1.03bn is slightly below the $1.04bn consensus.

Unchanged after hours. Gross margin was 85% in the quarter, revenue beat, and EPS was nearly $50 per share. The company announced an 8:1 stock split and bought back about $5bn of stock. Q4 revenue guidance is in line with the Street.

Flat after hours (-0.7%). Bears remain anchored to valuation and the sustainability of North America comps once the store closure and transferred sales are lapped. Bulls point to roughly 8% North America comps and margin beats.
Up 8% in the regular session, part of better restaurant fundamentals this week.

sector_views.rationale: Consumer names caught a larger bid on rotation out of tech and short covering in under-owned names (NCLH, CROX, BOOT). Restaurants showed better fundamentals (CMG, EAT, WING).
Tech sold off on underwhelming earnings (AMZN, GOOGL, INTC, PINS, TWLO), with the AI complex used as a source of funds.

earnings_insights: AMZN (reported 10/29 after close): AWS growth of 39% in the quarter vs consensus above 40%. Guidance in the press release is for AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028. Shares -10% after hours.
INTC (reported 10/29 after close): Q3 DCAI revenue +78% y/y. Q4 revenue guidance $15-16bn vs consensus $17.29bn. Shares -17% after hours.
PINS (reported 10/29 after close): Q3 revenue $1.17bn vs consensus $1.2bn. Q4 revenue and EBITDA guidance below Street. Shares -16% after hours.

SNDK (reported 10/29 after close): gross margin 85%, revenue beat, EPS nearly $50 per share. 8:1 stock split announced, about $5bn bought back in the quarter. Q4 revenue guidance in line with consensus. Shares unchanged after hours.

TWLO (reported 10/29 after close): Q3 organic revenue +16% y/y vs +17% in Q2. DBNER of 114%. Q4 organic growth guided to +11-12% y/y, in line with the initial Q3 organic guide. Shares -15% after hours.
RBLX (reported 10/29 after close): Q4 bookings guided down 10-15% y/y. Shares -10% after hours.

RDDT (reported 10/29 after close): Q3 revenue +53% y/y. US DAUs of 50.7mn, down from about 53mn last quarter. Q4 revenue guided to $1-1.03bn vs consensus $1.04bn. Shares -5% after hours, after being down 12%.

SBUX (reporting 10/29 after close): shares -0.7% after hours. North America comps of about 8% and margin beats noted. Bears focus on valuation and sustainability of North America comps after lapping store closures and transferred sales.
Google earnings (reported before 10/29 session) were described as disappointing and weighed on the AI trade. No figures are given in this note.

QQQ front-month fixed-strike vols were offered down about a vol point at the lows. SPY vols fell more than 80 bps of vol.
VIX futures moved nominally lower, which the desk reads as vol premium coming out of the market after several prominent tech prints.
Skew was bid on the move lower, particularly in SPX gamma tenors.
A customer bought 15k SPX 31Mar 5500 puts as a crash hedge.
In single stocks and thematics, clients hedged single-name tech exposure and added convexity (option protection that gains more as the move grows) only sparsely in higher-conviction positions.
MOC imbalance of $9bn to buy. Asset managers finished as slight net sellers, hedge fund flows were roughly flat, and SPX volume was about 35% above the 20-day average.
